chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they voluntarily surrendered of themselves.

key_terms.اسْتَحَلَّهُمْ: They made permissible for themselves / voluntarily surrendered

ai.seo_question: What is the source of Satan's power over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's authority is not inherent but contingent upon human free will, specifically when believers voluntarily surrender to his whispers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of *Ikhtiyar* (choice), affirming that divine decree does not negate human responsibility for spiritual decline. The narration serves as a crucial counter to deterministic views, emphasizing that obedience to Satan is a conscious act of submission rather than compulsion.
